title: Adjust the sum-to-infinity formula for a geometric series that starts at n=2 (or later) instead of n=1
content: The formula S∞ = a/(1-r) assumes the series starts at n=1 with first term a. If a sum instead starts at n=2 (or n=k for some k>1), you have two equally valid approaches: either (1) treat the term at n=2 as the new first term a' = ar (or more generally ar^(k-1)) and apply S∞ = a'/(1-r) directly, or (2) sum the whole series from n=1 using S∞ = a/(1-r), then subtract off the term(s) you don't want (e.g. subtract just the n=1 term to get the sum from n=2 onwards). Both routes give the same value — pick whichever makes the algebra with your particular a and r simplest.
